text: Files must be explicitly added to the chat context (via CLI args or /add) before aider can edit them
quote: To edit files, you need to “add them to the chat”. Do this by naming them on the aider command line. Or, you can use the in-chat `/add` command to add files.

text: Users can undo AI-made changes with an /undo command
quote: You can always use the `/undo` command to undo AI changes that you don’t like.

text: Aider automatically commits every AI edit with a descriptive commit message
quote: Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message. This makes it easy to undo or review aider’s changes.

text: Users can run raw git commands via /git for more complex git history management
quote: `/git` will let you run raw git commands to do more complex management of your git history.

text: A --message CLI argument lets you give a one-shot natural language instruction that aider executes and applies before exiting
quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.

text: A Python SDK (Coder.create/coder.run) lets developers script single coding instructions programmatically
quote:
coder = Coder.create(main_model=model, fnames=fnames)

# This will execute one instruction on those files and then return
coder.run("make a script that prints hello world")

text: Aider can run against local models such as those served via Ollama
quote: Aider can work also with local models, for example using [Ollama]

text: With --watch-files, aider watches repo files for AI coding instructions added in any editor and acts on them
quote: If you run aider with `--watch-files`, it will watch all files in your repo and look for any AI coding instructions you add using your favorite IDE or text editor.

text: /ask lets users query the codebase in natural language without making edits
quote: **/ask** Ask questions about the code base without editing any files.

text: Aider builds and can print a concise map of the whole repository, including key classes/functions and signatures
quote: Aider uses a **concise map of your whole git repository** that includes the most important classes and functions along with their types and call signatures.

text: Aider automatically lints any files it edits
quote: By default, aider will lint any files which it edits.

text: /test runs a specified test command and aider reads stdout/stderr and exit code to detect failures
quote: You can run tests with `/test <test-command>`. Aider will run the test command without any arguments. If there are test errors, aider expects the command to print them on stdout/stderr and return a non-zero exit code.

text: /run lets users execute code from chat and optionally feed the output back to aider
quote: You can use the `/run` command in the chat to run your code and optionally share the output with aider.

text: An experimental browser-based UI lets users collaborate with LLMs to edit code in a local git repo
quote: Use aider’s new experimental browser UI to collaborate with LLMs to edit code in your local git repo.

text: A /voice command records spoken instructions and transcribes them as chat input for coding
quote: Use the in-chat `/voice` command to start recording, and press `ENTER` when you’re done speaking. Your voice coding instructions will be transcribed, as if you had typed them into the aider chat session.

text: Options can be configured via CLI switches, a YAML config file, or AIDER_ environment variables
quote: Aider has many options which can be set with command line switches. Most options can also be set in an `.aider.conf.yml` file... Or by setting environment variables like `AIDER_xxx`

text: /architect mode uses two separate models (architect + editor) together for a task
quote: **/architect** Enter architect/editor mode using 2 different models. If no prompt provided, switches to architect/editor mode.

text: /web scrapes a webpage, converts it to markdown, and inserts it into the chat
quote: **/web** Scrape a webpage, convert to markdown and send in a message

text: Aider supports a copy/paste workflow to use any web chat LLM interface instead of an API
quote:
### Copy/paste to web chat

Aider works best with LLM APIs, but it can also work an LLM via its web chat interface. Aider streamlines copy/pasting code back and forth with a browser.

text: Users can add images and web pages to the chat as visual/reference context
quote: Add images and web pages to the chat to provide visual context, screenshots, reference docs, etc.

text: Aider supports most popular programming languages including python, javascript, rust, ruby, go, cpp, php, html, css and more
quote: Aider works with most popular programming languages: python, javascript, rust, ruby, go, cpp, php, html, css, and dozens more.
